### Review Cycle Time

> The journal's own pages give three differing figures. The dedicated review-process page (https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/page/review-process) says stage one usually takes 12 to 16 weeks and stage two an additional 12 to 16 weeks. The guidelines page (https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/page/guidelines-for-authors) says 6 to 10 weeks for stage one and about 12 additional weeks for stage two, and adds that the process is "taking up to 6 weeks longer than normal" because of volume. Which is current is not stated; both retrieved 2026-11-23. The Article Submission FAQ (Wayback copy captured 2026-08-31, which shows the 2025-2026 editorial board; https://web.archive.org/web/20260831092228id_/https://hep.gse.harvard.edu/journals/about-harvard-educational-review/) says that, because of high volume and editorial turnover, review is "currently taking up to 14 weeks" for stage one plus an additional 12 weeks for stage two, against a standard of 6 to 10 weeks for stage one plus 12 weeks for stage two. Reconciliation: for stage one the FAQ's current "up to 14" lies inside the review-process page's 12 to 16 and inside the guidelines page's 6 to 10 plus up to 6 weeks of delay (up to 16); for stage two the FAQ's 12 weeks matches the guidelines page's about 12 and is below the review-process page's 12 to 16. The FAQ's "standard" figures (6 to 10 and 12) are the guidelines page's, so the guidelines and FAQ pages agree with each other and the review-process page is the outlier; this is a reading of three undated statements, not a journal statement of which is current.

| Stage | Typical Time | Notes |
|-------|-------------|-------|
| **Time to first decision** | 12 to 16 weeks (review-process page), or 6 to 10 weeks plus up to 6 weeks of delay (guidelines page), or "up to 14 weeks" currently with a standard of 6 to 10 weeks (FAQ, Wayback copy captured 2026-08-31, https://web.archive.org/web/20260831092228id_/https://hep.gse.harvard.edu/journals/about-harvard-educational-review/) for stage one | Publisher-reported, no period stated |
| **Time to first review** | Blank. No separate figure on either page | |
| **Time to acceptance (total)** | Stage one plus stage two: 24 to 32 weeks on the review-process page, about 18 to 22 weeks plus delay on the guidelines page, and 26 weeks currently (14 + 12) or 18 to 22 weeks standard on the FAQ page (sums of the stated stage durations; no total is stated by the journal). SciRev has 0 reviews (https://scirev.org/reviews/harvard-educational-review/) and LetPub shows 0 reviews (https://www.letpub.com/journal-selector/journal/11721) | Arithmetic on stated stages |
| **Time to publication (after acceptance)** | The FAQ (Wayback copy captured 2026-08-31, https://web.archive.org/web/20260831092228id_/https://hep.gse.harvard.edu/journals/about-harvard-educational-review/) says the date depends on how many manuscripts are in the queue for an issue and that it "typically" takes about 6 months after acceptance. The review-process page says only that the date depends on the queue for upcoming issues | Publisher-reported; copy 2026-08-31 |

## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Author-anonymised, two-stage review run by the journal's own editorial board of doctoral students. Preliminary screening by the manuscripts editor; stage one read by at least two board members; stage two read by the full board at weekly meetings. Manuscripts must be anonymised (author-identifying citations changed to "Author"). Sources: https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/page/review-process and https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/page/guidelines-for-authors ; the board page describes first-year duties as "blind peer review" (https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/page/editorial-board). Retrieved 2026-11-23. No page read describes external referees. The FAQ (Wayback copy captured 2026-08-31, https://web.archive.org/web/20260831092228id_/https://hep.gse.harvard.edu/journals/about-harvard-educational-review/) lists the possible decisions as Accept, Accept with Revisions, Revise and Return, or Reject |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No source found |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Not as described on any page read. Authors whose manuscripts reach stage two receive written feedback based on the board's discussion; stage-one rejections get no detailed comments (https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/page/review-process) |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Blank. The submission portal has a category for revised and resubmitted manuscripts, open only to manuscripts the board invited for revision (https://hepg.submittable.com/submit, read through a fetch tool, retrieved 2026-11-23); the number of rounds is not stated |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. No source found |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Yes: a dedicated section on generative AI tools in the author guidelines |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | Disclosure gate: all uses must be disclosed, and the Editorial Board reviews each disclosure "to assess the legitimacy" of the reported use. No pre-approval step is described |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 2 (disclosure required and board-reviewed; only non-substantive uses permitted; same rubric as the Mind entry, where 3 is allowed with mandatory disclosure) |
| **Summary** | Tools cannot be credited as co-authors. Permitted: language refinement and editing, grammar and spelling, translation assistance for language refinement, formatting. Prohibited: creating or manipulating original data and results, producing written text for the manuscript, creating new images or figures. Authors upload an anonymised disclosure document and add a short acknowledgment at the end of the manuscript saying which tools were used, how and why. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/page/guidelines-for-authors |

## Format

> Source: https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/page/guidelines-for-authors unless stated; retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Research Articles, Essays, Voices (reflective accounts of education), and Additional Submissions for work that fits none of these. The portal also lists revised-and-resubmitted, solicited and invited manuscripts (https://hepg.submittable.com/submit). OpenAlex types for the window: 148 articles, 41 book reviews, 4 editorials, 1 erratum |
| **Word limit** | Up to 9,000 words including abstract, appendices and references; the journal reserves the right to return longer manuscripts. A reading of the portal page says no minimum, with accepted manuscripts tending to run at least 5,500 words (https://hepg.submittable.com/submit, fetch-tool summary of the page); for the disability special issue, Voices pieces are limited to 5,500 words (https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/content/call-abstracts-and-manuscripts) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The guidelines state a return right and no exception route |
| **Abstract limit** | 250 words maximum; at most six keywords taken from the ERIC descriptor list, with one or two free keywords allowed |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap; references count inside the 9,000 words |
| **Supplementary material** | Appendices count inside the 9,000 words. No other supplementary-file rule found. Written permission documents for copyrighted figures, tables or extended quotations must accompany the submission |
| **Figure/Table limits** | Blank. No count limit found on the guidelines page |
| **Style / submission format** | One Word file with all components (no PDFs); file named by manuscript title; no title page; double-spaced, at least 12 point, 1-inch margins, numbered pages; APA 7th edition for references (other styles are returned); Chicago Manual of Style for general style; journal defers to author preference on naming racial, ethnic and cultural groups |
| **Additional-submission statement** | The guidelines ask for a statement of up to 100 words describing an additional submission; a fetch-tool reading of the portal page says 500 words. The two pages disagree and the discrepancy was not resolved |

The guidelines welcome accounts "from settings in the United States and abroad" (https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/page/guidelines-for-authors) |

Countries are not listed per editor, so no country split is given; bios mention prior degrees from the United States, the United Arab Emirates and France among others |

The aims page states a commitment to "social justice scholarship" and encourages BIPOC authors, authors of other underrepresented identities and early-career scholars (https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/page/about/aims%20and%20scope) |

Terms in title or abstract: "racism" 17, "critical race theory" 6, "social justice" 6 of 154 records with an abstract (OpenAlex stemmed-search figure; title-only numerator caveat). The most-cited 2021-2026 articles in OpenAlex are, however, on platforms and data in education: https://doi.org/10.17763/1943-5045-92.2.284 (145 citations), https://doi.org/10.17763/1943-5045-92.2.209 (112), https://doi.org/10.17763/1943-5045-92.2.231 (109), https://doi.org/10.17763/1943-5045-92.4.566a (103) and https://doi.org/10.17763/1943-5045-92.2.257 (85); retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Stated political position** | The aims page says the editorial policy does not reflect an official position of Harvard's education faculty, and states the board's commitment to advancing equity and social-justice scholarship (aims URL above). The special-issue call states that it seeks scholarship only from people with lived disability experience or close ties to disability communities (https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/content/call-abstracts-and-manuscripts) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Three stated expectations in the guidelines (https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/page/guidelines-for-authors, retrieved 2026-11-23): the questions must be relevant to education and carry implications for broader educational problems; the manuscript must state its theoretical or practical contribution and who benefits; and the writing must suit a generalist readership, in clear language without technical jargon.
- **What kind of engagement?** Authors are encouraged across all submissions to discuss how their identity and positionality may have shaped the agenda, methods, data analysis and findings (guidelines page). The publication criteria add that a manuscript should push theory in a new direction, fill a gap or bring a new perspective.
- **Article types and their expected shape**: Research Articles should contain background or framework, literature review, methods, findings and analysis, and discussion; Essays need an argument that advances or synthesises rather than summarises; Voices pieces rest on the author's voice and grounding in practice (guidelines page). Up to 9,000 words with a 250-word abstract (guidelines page).
- **Current call**: special issue on disability and special education, seeking historical, critical and disability-led work; abstracts of 250 words due 2027-01-01 and manuscripts due 2027-02-15 (https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/content/call-abstracts-and-manuscripts).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: the guidelines state that over-length manuscripts may be returned and that manuscripts with non-APA references are returned (guidelines page). No source states what happens to out-of-scope submissions, and no desk-rejection data exists (SciRev 0 reviews: https://scirev.org/reviews/harvard-educational-review/).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts: OpenAlex works of this source dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23, title or abstract match (stemmed), 194 records of which 154 have an abstract; shares use 154 as denominator. These shares are OpenAlex stemmed-search figures, not word-boundary regex counts: stemming widens what a term matches, and the numerator can include title-only matches from the 40 records that have no abstract while the denominator is the 154 records with an abstract, so a share can be overstated; they are not directly comparable with the Crossref title counts. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. Crossref gives a second, title-only check (185 records, no abstracts).

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 2 | "quantitative" 4 (2.6%), "survey" 5 (3.2%), "randomized" 0 (OpenAlex stemmed search, 154 records with an abstract; title-only numerator caveat); Crossref titles with experiment, randomised or statistics terms: 0 of 185. The special-issue call criticises dominant special-education research for favouring large-scale quantitative studies (https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/content/call-abstracts-and-manuscripts); that is a call-specific stance, not a general rule |
| Qualitative interviews | 3 | "interview" 24 (15.6%; includes some interview-format pieces), "qualitative" 8 (5.2%) (OpenAlex stemmed search, 154 records with an abstract; title-only numerator caveat) |
| Autoethnography | 1 | OpenAlex count not obtained (rate limit reached). Crossref titles: 1 of 185 (0.5%). The special-issue call names autoethnography and action research among welcomed methodologies (https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/content/call-abstracts-and-manuscripts) |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | "theoretical" 10 (6.5%), "essay" 42 (27.3%), "philosophical" 2 (1.3%) of 154 records with an abstract (OpenAlex stemmed-search figure; title-only numerator caveat); Essays are a full submission category (https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/page/guidelines-for-authors) |
| Mixed methods | 2 | "mixed methods" 2 (1.3%) of 154 records with an abstract (OpenAlex stemmed-search figure; title-only numerator caveat) (OpenAlex) |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 0 | "systematic review" 0 and "meta-analysis" 0 of 154 records with an abstract (OpenAlex stemmed-search figure; title-only numerator caveat) (OpenAlex); Crossref titles 0 of 185. Literature reviews are listed as one form an essay can take (guidelines page) |
| Historical (added row) | 3 | "historical" 21 (13.6%) of 154 records with an abstract (OpenAlex stemmed-search figure; title-only numerator caveat) (OpenAlex); the special-issue call lists historical methods first among its three areas |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewer behaviour itself is not observable from public pages; what follows is what public pages do show.

| Aspect | Detail | Evidence |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **Dominant tradition** | Review is carried out by the journal's own board of Harvard doctoral students rather than by an external referee pool as far as the pages read show. The 2026-2027 board lists 11 editors (9 PhD, 2 Ed.L.D.) with research interests spanning teacher education, special-education history, immigration law, computing education, policy, sociology and critical theory | https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/page/editorial-board , retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Reviewer list size** | Groups of 10 to 14 doctoral students work together on policy and manuscript evaluation; editors serve two-year terms; the board is selected through a competitive application process and advised by Harvard Graduate School of Education faculty and Harvard Education Publishing Group staff | Same board page |
| **Review model** | Anonymised manuscripts; screening by the manuscripts editor; stage one by at least two board members; stage two by the full board at weekly meetings | https://www.harvardeducationalreview.org/page/review-process |
| **Reviewer competence variance** | Blank. No first-hand report exists: SciRev 0 reviews, LetPub 0 reviews | https://scirev.org/reviews/harvard-educational-review/ ; https://www.letpub.com/journal-selector/journal/11721 |
| **Quantitative mindset bias on qualitative work?** | Blank. No source. Qualitative terms are far more frequent than quantitative ones in the journal's output (OpenAlex counts under Methodological Preferences), which cannot show how any reviewer treats either | OpenAlex counts, see Methodological Preferences |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it.

### Hard Blockers

- **Length**: up to 9,000 words including abstract, appendices and references; the journal reserves the right to return longer manuscripts (Format; guidelines page).
- **Reference style**: APA 7th edition; other styles are returned (Format).
- **Public posting**: manuscripts must be removed from public websites before submission, and simultaneous consideration elsewhere is barred (Preprint Policy; Practical Concerns).
- **AI use**: undisclosed use, or AI-produced text, data or images, breach the stated policy (AI Policy).
- **Anonymisation**: manuscripts with identifying self-citations or a title page do not meet the stated preparation rules (Format; Practical Concerns).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact read; ethics-approval and data-sharing rules were not found.

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the journal's own pages give 12 to 16 weeks for stage one and as much again for stage two, or 6 to 10 plus about 12 weeks with a stated volume delay, or currently up to 14 weeks plus 12 on the FAQ page (Review Cycle Time). The stated figures differ, and no total is given; the FAQ also says publication typically follows acceptance by about 6 months.
- **Feedback**: stage-one rejections receive no detailed comments (Peer Review), so a rejection may carry no usable guidance.
- **Generalist register**: the guidelines require jargon-free writing for a generalist audience and encourage positionality statements (Framing Requirements; Voice & Style); work written for a specialist subfield needs rewriting for this register.
- **Open submission windows**: invitations are paused and the two pages give different resumption dates (Practical Concerns); open-call submission continues.
- **Access to the published version**: subscription, online-only; public posting of the full text is not allowed (Open Access; Preprint Policy).

### Best Suited For

- Essays and conceptual or historical arguments about education: "essay" 42 and "historical" 21 of 154 records with an abstract (OpenAlex stemmed-search figure; title-only numerator caveat), and Essays is a named category (Methodological Preferences; Format).
- Qualitative or ethnographic work with a clear equity or social-justice framing: "interview" 24, "ethnography" 10, "racism" 17, primary topic Critical Race Theory in Education 33 of 194 (Methodological Preferences; Epistemological & Political Leanings), and the aims statement (Sensitive Topics).
- Practitioner and community voices: a dedicated Voices category with its own length rules (Format).
- Early-career and underrepresented authors, which the aims page explicitly encourages (Epistemological & Political Leanings); this says nothing about acceptance odds.
- Disability-led or historical special-education scholarship in the current special issue (Framing Requirements).

### Not Recommended For

- Quantitative experimental studies or systematic reviews as the main contribution: "randomized" 0, "systematic review" 0, "meta-analysis" 0 of 154 records with an abstract (OpenAlex stemmed-search figure; title-only numerator caveat), "quantitative" 4 (Methodological Preferences). The counts show these are rare here, not that they are rejected.
- Authors who need a preprint or public draft in circulation during review: the stated rule requires removal from public sites before submission (Preprint Policy).
- Authors needing a firm timeline: the journal's two pages give different durations and no total (Review Cycle Time).
- Highly specialised technical writing: the stated audience is generalist (Voice & Style).
